correctness.rationale: For the finite linear word (0^a1^b)^m with a,b,m at least two, the singleton factors force one position per symbol. The 01 and 10 tests require, respectively, an internal-block boundary endpoint and an inter-block boundary endpoint. The first and last positions of each constant run are distinct, leaving just the two stated families. For sufficiency of a last-position pair, the first change of any mixed factor fixes its start residue r modulo p=a+b. If its length is at least p-r, it reaches the last one of its starting block. Place the occurrence in the chosen one's block if that start fits; otherwise the rightmost occurrence starts before that position and ends at least at (m-1)p, since less than one period can be left unused on its right. If the length is smaller than p-r it must start with zeros, cross 01, and fit in the chosen zero's block. Constant factors fit through the selected run ends, and reversal with complementation maps the first-position family to the last-position family with run lengths swapped. Thus the boundary restrictions, optimal size and count 2m(m-1) all follow. An independent occurrence-interval program checked every candidate pair and the four-test equivalence for 30 parameter triples; replay: python3 /workspace/branches/exact_review_checks.py 5. The frozen checker and its output were inspected, not executed; both finite checks are corroborative, not the proof.
residual_risks: No assertion for circular words, a single period, or run lengths one is needed for the frozen proof.
